solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sad call after falling over on road

indicators.note: in an across clue, placed on means coming after the other piece

parts.note: a path is a minor road or track

indicators.note: toppling over means the word for call is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: to cite is to call, as a witness is cited or called

explanation.surface: Someone is miserable after a fall in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling over' makes ETIC; in an across answer 'on' means following, so the road comes first. 'Sad' here means pitiable rather than unhappy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathetic describes something pitiful, which arouses sorrow and so can mean sad.

clue.text: Remain attached to a daughter wanting present

parts.note: here means present, as when answering a roll call

explanation.surface: A girl wants her daughter to stay clinging to her.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick or stay fixed to something, the same verb sense.

clue.text: Ducks invading hospital repeateadly, ending with a commotion

indicators.note: the zeros invade, that is go inside, the pair of hospital letters
repeatedly (as printed, misspelt) means said again, so the hospital letter appears twice over

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so two ducks are two O's

explanation.surface: Ducks keep barging into a hospital, causing a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeateadly' (a misprint of repeatedly) doubles H to HH, and 'invading' puts OO inside it to give HOOH; 'ending with' then adds the A. A duck is a nil score in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoo-ha is informal British slang for a noisy fuss or commotion.

clue.text: The rest is made into garments

indicators.note: the words are reshaped into something new, an instruction to rearrange their letters

explanation.surface: The remaining fabric is turned into clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made into' rearranges the letters of THE REST IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tee shirts are casual collarless tops, a kind of garment.

clue.text: Country to get upset under Conservative clique

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means placed below and so after the other piece
upset means overturned, so in a down clue both words are flipped and read upwards

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nation is angered under a Tory government's inner circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get upset' turns EIRE TO into OTERIE, which goes 'under' C.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive group of people, the same as a clique.

clue.text: One might be greatly distressed losing this VIP

definitions.text: One might be greatly distressed losing this
definitions.meaning: read distressed as dis-tressed: lose a large hairpiece and you have lost your tresses
an important person, a big shot

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: 'distressed' is read as 'without tresses', which is what a person would be after losing a large wig.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigwig is an informal term for an important person, a very important person.

clue.text: Groom to hurry after bride initially

indicators.note: the hurrying word is placed after the bride's letter
initially means take just the first letter of the word bride

parts.note: to rush is to hurry

explanation.surface: A groom hurries off after his bride at a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives B from 'bride', and 'after' puts RUSH behind it. 'Groom' is the verb, as in grooming a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To groom an animal is to brush its coat, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Final message worthy warrior's spoken

indicators.note: spoken means the phrase is heard rather than read, so it is a soundalike

parts.note: good means worthy or virtuous; a knight is a medieval warrior

explanation.surface: A virtuous fighter delivers his last words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoken' tells you GOOD KNIGHT is heard, and it gives a word spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: A goodnight is the last thing said at the end of an evening, a farewell message.

clue.text: Home's lofty architectural feature on top of dome is outstanding

parts.note: in means at home; the apostrophe s is just a link meaning has, as in home has
a spire is the tall tapering top of a church tower

indicators.note: top of means only the uppermost, first letter of the word dome

explanation.surface: A house's tall spire set atop its dome is remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home' gives IN (at home). 'top of' takes the D of 'dome'; 'on' places SPIRE above it in the down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspired work is exceptionally good, so it can be called outstanding.

clue.text: This is lacking? Then king must be given one!

definitions.text: This is lacking? Then king must be given one!

indicators.note: lacking means the word is taken away from the word before it

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from the Latin rex
taken as written

explanation.surface: If this is missing, then the king needs one provided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' takes IS out of THIS to leave TH. Read as a whole, the clue also describes the answer: a king without one must be given one.
explanation.definitionFit: A throne is the seat a monarch needs, which is what the whole clue describes.

clue.text: French city chucked out undesirable person

indicators.note: chucked means thrown about, so the letters of out are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: a louse is a contemptible, undesirable person

explanation.surface: A town in France threw out an unwanted visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chucked' makes TOU. 'undesirable person' looks like the thing thrown out, but it is a piece of the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Toulouse is a large city in south-west France.

clue.text: About to enter city, about to return for a quick break

indicators.note: to enter means to go inside, so this word goes inside the city

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: to return means to go back, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: re again means about

explanation.surface: Someone is about to go into town and about to come home, for a quick pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' makes BREATH and 'to return' makes ER. Bath is a Roman spa city in south-west England; 'About' is used twice, in the same sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A breather is a short rest or pause, a quick break from effort.

clue.text: Chinese dynasty having the spirit not to give up

parts.note: the Han were an ancient Chinese dynasty
gin is a spirit, the drink

explanation.surface: An ancient Chinese ruling house had the strength of will to persevere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' looks like determination; here it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang in is an idiom meaning to persist and not quit.

clue.text: The sort of opportunist vicar Peter appears to be!

definitions.text: The sort of opportunist vicar Peter appears to be!

parts.words: The sort of opportunist vicar Peter appears to be!
parts.note: the phrase vicar Peter has a floor covering bagged inside it, from the end of vicar through the start of Peter, so it is literally a bagger of one

explanation.walkthrough: The opportunist meant is an outsider who moves in to exploit a place. The cryptic half is that 'viCAR PETer' holds, or bags, a floor covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpetbagger is an opportunist who exploits a place or organisation they have no real tie to.

clue.text: Get firm with maiden — and loud, right? Not maybe if she needs this!

definitions.text: Get firm with maiden — and loud, right? Not maybe if she needs this!

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
forte is the musical term for loud

explanation.surface: Should one be stern and loud with a young woman? Not if she needs soothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a girl who needs consoling should not be treated firmly and loudly. A maiden is an over with no runs in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A comforter is someone or something that consoles, what a distressed young woman would need instead of harshness.

clue.text: French cheese a fashionable mum introduced as something for the kitchen

indicators.note: introduced means brought in, so these letters go inside the cheese

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
in means fashionable
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A trendy mother brings in some French cheese for the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduced' makes B-AINMA-RIE. 'French cheese' looks like the subject; it is the outer shell of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bain-marie is a pan of hot water in which dishes are gently heated, a kitchen utensil.

clue.text: Study awful rot written about church music

parts.note: to con is to study or learn, as in conning a part
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: awful means dreadful, a sign that the letters are in a mess and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic studies terrible church music and writes that it is rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' makes CERTO; 'written about' is only a link. CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A concerto is a piece of music for a solo instrument with orchestra.

clue.text: Maoist racism possibly observable in old-style Soviet department

indicators.note: possibly means the letters could be arranged another way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Racism in Maoist thought may be seen in an old Soviet ministry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges MAOIST RACISM.
explanation.definitionFit: A commissariat was a government department in the Soviet Union, run by a commissar.

clue.text: A sitter in peculiar guise — most pretentious

indicators.note: in an odd disguise means the letters of sitter appear rearranged

explanation.surface: A model posing for a painter wears a strange disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in peculiar guise' makes RTIEST. 'sitter' suggests an artist's model, which fits the arty answer's surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty means affectedly artistic, so the superlative means most pretentious.

clue.text: Playful little woman joining sailor in church

parts.note: Jo is one of the sisters in the novel Little Women

indicators.note: in means the sailor goes inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
OS stands for ordinary seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A cheerful young woman meets a sailor in church.
explanation.walkthrough: Jo March is a sister in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women. 'in' makes COSE; 'joining' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Jocose means jocular or humorous, so it is a synonym of playful.

clue.text: Move through text to get first two bits of school list

indicators.note: the first two bits means only the opening pair of letters of the word school

parts.note: a roll is a list of names, as in a school roll

explanation.surface: You can browse a school's list on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first two bits of' makes SC. A school roll is the register of pupils, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To scroll is to move up or down through text on a screen.

clue.text: Reluctant to hate, lacking the energy

indicators.note: lacking means the energy letter is taken away from the hating word

parts.note: to loathe is to hate
E is the abbreviation for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Someone is unwilling to hate because they lack the energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' takes E out of LOATHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Loath is an adjective meaning unwilling or reluctant.

clue.text: Newspaper group coming together for a limited period

parts.note: The Times is a British newspaper
a lot is a group or set of things

explanation.surface: A newspaper group merges for a short time.
explanation.walkthrough: THE TIMES is a London daily newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A time slot is an allotted period in a schedule, a limited period.

clue.text: Like certain rays that could be blocked by parasol, arguably

indicators.note: blocked by means kept inside the words parasol and arguably, which hold the answer in their letters

explanation.surface: A sunshade might arguably keep out some of the sun's rays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocked by' finds the answer inside 'paraSOL ARguably'. The surface reading also fits: a parasol blocks the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Solar means relating to the sun, so solar rays are the sun's rays.

clue.text: Chemical has upset aunt here

indicators.note: upset means disturbed or knocked over, a sign to rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: An aunt has been distressed by a chemical in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges AUNT HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Urethane is an organic compound used in making plastics, a chemical.

clue.text: We can't wait to have a certain type of cosmetic!

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of eagerness for something to come sooner
a deodorant or lotion applied with a rolling ball

explanation.definitionFit: Roll on is said when longing for a future event; a roll-on is a cosmetic in a ball-tipped bottle.

clue.text: Musical interval outside for people to listen to

indicators.note: said for an audience to hear means a soundalike, a word spelt differently

parts.note: forth means out or into the open, outside

explanation.surface: A musical interval is performed outdoors for an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for people to listen to' says FORTH is heard, giving a word that sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A fourth is the interval spanning four notes of a diatonic scale.

clue.text: Party members full of explosive suppositions

indicators.note: full of means containing, so the explosive goes inside the party members

parts.note: Tories are members of the British Conservative Party
HE is short for high explosive

explanation.surface: Members of a party are packed with explosive ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of' puts the explosive inside the party. Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party; 'explosive' looks like an adjective but is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Theories are ideas proposed to explain things, much the same as suppositions.
